div.p: Greetings, sons and daughters, in the name of the Lord who loved us, in peace.

Since the ordinances of God toward you are great and rich, I rejoice exceedingly and beyond measure over your blessed and glorious spirits; so οὕτω L, ουτο ℵ, οὗ τό C.innately have you received the grace of the spiritual gift.

Wherefore I also congratulate myself the more, hoping to be saved, because I truly see in you the Spirit poured out upon you from the richness of the fountain of the Lord. So greatly has your much-desired sight of you amazed me.

Being convinced of this, then, and conscious within myself that having spoken much among you I know that the Lord journeyed with me in the way of righteousness, I am wholly constrained to this also, to love you more than my own soul, because great faith and Tit. 1, 2; 3, 7love dwell in you in the hope of his life.

Considering this, therefore, that if I take care for you to share some part of what I have received, my service to such spirits will be to my reward, I have hastened to send you a brief letter,
so that along with your faith you may have perfect knowledge. Tit. 1, 2; 3, 7

There are, then, three doctrines of the Lord: the hope of life, the beginning and end of our faith; righteousness, the beginning and end of judgment; and love, the witness of gladness and exultation in works of righteousness. The text of this whole passage is confused: tres sunt ergo constitutiones domini, vitae spes initium et consummatio L and no more; τρία οὖν δόγματά ἐστιν κυρίου, ζωή, πίστις, ἐλπίς, ἀρχὴ καὶ τέλος ἡμῶν, καὶ δικεοσύνη κρίσεως ἀρχή, καὶ τέλος ἀγάπη, εὐφροσύνη, καὶ ἀγαλλιάσεως ἔργων ἐν δικαιοσύναις μαρτυρία ℵ. The text printed is that of C, which gives the best sense, though it is doubtful if it is more than the correction of an early corruption.

For the Master has made known to us through the prophets things past and things present, and has given us firstfruits of the taste of things to come; and seeing these things coming to pass one by one, just as he spoke, we ought to draw near to his fear more richly and more loftily.
Yet I, not as a teacher, but as one of yourselves, will show you a few things through which you may be gladdened in the present circumstances.
Since the days are evil, therefore, and the worker of evil himself holds power, we ought to attend to ourselves and seek out the ordinances of the Lord.
Now the helpers of our faith are fear and endurance, and our allies are longsuffering and self-control;

while these remain pure in the things pertaining to the Lord, there rejoice
with them wisdom, understanding, skill, and knowledge.
For he has made plain to us through all the prophets that he needs neither sacrifices nor burnt offerings nor oblations, saying in one place:

What to me is the multitude Is. 1, 1-13of your sacrifices? says the Lord. I am full of burnt offerings, and I do not desire the fat of lambs or the blood of bulls and goats, nor that you should come to appear before me; for who has required these things at your hands? You shall no longer tread my court. If you bring fine flour, it is vain; incense is an abomination to me; your new moons and sabbaths I cannot endure.
These things, then, he abolished, so that the new law of our Lord Jesus Christ, which is without the yoke of necessity, might not have a human-made offering.
And again he says to them: Did I command your fathers when they came out Jer. 7. 22, 23of the land of Egypt to offer me burnt offerings and sacrifices?
Rather, this is what I commanded them: Let none of you Zech 8, 17bear a grudge of evil in his heart against his neighbor, and do not love a false oath.

We ought therefore to perceive, not being without understanding, the loving purpose of our Father; for he speaks to us, desiring that we should not go astray like Ps. 51, 19them in seeking how we may approach him.

To us, then, he speaks thus: A sacrifice to the Lord τῶ κυρίῳ CL, τῶ θεῳ ℵ (LXX).is a broken heart; a savor of sweet fragrance to the Lord is a heart that glorifies him who fashioned it. We ought therefore, brethren, to be very careful concerning our salvation, lest
the Evil One, having made an infiltration of error among us, should hurl us away from our life.

Is. 58, 4, 5Again, therefore, he speaks to them concerning these things: Why do you fast for me, says the Lord, so that your voice is heard today in clamor? This is not the fast that I have chosen, says the Lord, not a man humbling his soul,
nor even if you bend your neck like a ring and put on sackcloth and spread ashes beneath you—not even so shall you call it an acceptable fast.

But to us Is. 58, 6-10he says: Behold, this is the fast that I have chosen, says the Lord: loose every bond of wickedness, untie the knots of oppressive contracts, send the crushed away in freedom, and tear up every unjust agreement. Break your bread for the hungry, and if you see one naked, clothe him; bring the homeless into your house, and if you see a humble man, you shall not despise him, nor any of the kindred of your own seed.

Then shall your light break forth early, and your garments ἱμάτια ℵ* CL, ἱάματα ℵ Corr. (healings) (LXX). This correction, which Lightfoot accepts, is no doubt what Barnabas meant, but the MSS. evidence suggests that it is not what he wrote.shall spring up speedily, and righteousness shall go before you, and the glory of God shall encompass you.

Then you shall cry out, and God will hear you; while you are still speaking he will say: Behold, I am here—if you remove
from yourself the bond and the pointing of the finger and the word of murmuring, and give your bread to the hungry from your heart and have mercy on a humbled soul.

For this reason, therefore, brethren, the Longsuffering One, foreseeing that the people whom he prepared in his Beloved would believe in sincerity, revealed all things to us beforehand, so that we should not shipwreck ourselves as proselytes ἐπήλυτοι ℵ, προσήλυτοι C, proselytae L; the use of the words in Philo suggests that they both mean proselytes, so that the evidence of L is ambiguous.upon their law.

We must therefore inquire deeply ἐραυνῶντας ℵ, ἐρευνῶντας C.concerning present things and seek out what is able to save us. Let us then flee completely from all the works of lawlessness, lest the works of lawlessness overtake us; and let us hate the error of the present time, that we may be loved in the time to come.
Let us give no relaxation to our soul so that it should have liberty to run with sinners and wicked men, lest we become like them.

The final stumbling-block has drawn near, of which it is written, as Enoch Enoch, 80, 61-64; 90, 17says. For to this end the Master has cut short the times and the days, that his Beloved may hasten and come to his inheritance. Dan. 7, 24
And thus also says the prophet: Ten kingdoms shall reign upon the earth, and after them ὄπισθεν CL, ὄπισθεν αὐτῶν ℵ (Theod.).shall arise a little king, who shall humble three of the kings at once.

Likewise concerning the
Dan. 7, 7. 8same says Daniel: And I saw the fourth beast, wicked and strong and fiercer than all the beasts of the sea, θαλάσσης CL, γῆς ℵ.and how from it sprang up ten horns, and from among them a little horn, an offshoot, and how it humbled at once three of the great horns.

You ought therefore to understand. And this further I ask of you, as one of yourselves, Didache ii, 7and loving you all individually more than my own soul: take heed to yourselves now and do not become like certain people, heaping up your sins and saying that the covenant is both theirs and ours.

Ours indeed it is; but they lost it completely in this manner when Moses had just received it. Exod. 84, 28For Scripture says: And Moses was in the mountain fasting forty days and forty nights, and he received the Exod. 32, 16covenant from the Lord, tablets of stone written with the finger of the hand of the Lord.

But by turning to idols they lost it. Exod. 32, 7 Deut. 9, 12For thus says the Lord: Moses, Moses, go down quickly, for your people whom you brought out of the land of Egypt have acted lawlessly. And Moses understood, and cast the two tablets out of his hands; and their covenant was broken, so that the covenant of the beloved Jesus might be sealed in our heart in the hope of faith in him.

Now though I wish to write many things, not as a teacher, but as befits one who loves you not to omit anything of what we possess, I have hastened to write as your devoted servant. Therefore let us take heed in the last days; for
Didache xvi. 2the whole time of our faith τῆς πίστεως ἡμῶν ℵ, τῆς ζωῆς ἡμῶν C, vitae nostrae et fidei L.will profit us nothing unless now, in the lawless time and the coming stumbling-blocks, we resist as befits sons of God, so that ἴνα ℵ, ἴνα οὖν C, ἴνα . . . μέλας om. L.the Black One may find no way of entry.

Let us flee from all vanity; let us utterly hate the works of the evil way. Do not live apart by yourselves, retiring into solitude as if already justified, but coming together into one place, inquire together concerning the common good.

For Scripture Is. 5, 21says: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight. Let us become spiritual; let us become a perfect temple to God. So far as lies in Is. 33, 18us, let us meditate on the fear of God and strive to keep his commandments, so that we may rejoice in his ordinances.

The Lord I. Pet. 1, 17, cf. Rom. 2. 11; Gal. 2, 6 II Cor. 5, 10will judge the world without partiality. Each shall receive according to what he has done: if he is good, his righteousness will go before him; if he is wicked, the reward of wickedness is before him;
so that we may never, resting at ease as the called, fall asleep in our sins, and the wicked ruler, gaining power over us, thrust us out from the kingdom of the Lord.

And consider this further, my brethren: when you see that after such great signs and wonders were wrought in Israel they were still abandoned thus, Mt. 20, 16: 22, 14let us take heed lest, as it is written, we be found many called, but few chosen.

For to this end the Lord endured to deliver up his flesh to destruction, that we might be cleansed by the forgiveness of sins, which is in the blood of his sprinkling. αἵματι τοῦ ῥαντίσματος αὐτοῦ ℵ, ῥαντίσματι αὐτοῦ τού αἵματος CL, a natural correction of the more difficult phrase.

For it is written concerning him, partly with reference to Israel and partly to Is. 53, 5. 7us, and it speaks thus: He was wounded for our transgressions and bruised for our sins; by his stripes we were healed; as a sheep he was led to the slaughter, and as a lamb silent before its shearer.

We ought therefore to give exceeding thanks to the Lord, because he has both made known to us things past and made us wise in things present, and we are not without understanding for things to come. Prov. 1, 17
Now Scripture says: Not unjustly are nets spread for birds. This means that a man will justly perish who, having knowledge of the way of righteousness, keeps himself back in the way of darkness.

And this further, my brethren: if the Lord endured to suffer for our soul, being Lord of the whole world, to whom God Gen. 1, 26said from the foundation of the world: Let us make man according to our image and likeness—how then did he endure to suffer at the hand of men?

Learn: the prophets, having their grace from him, prophesied concerning him; and he himself, in order to II Tim. 1, 10abolish death and show the resurrection from the dead, I Tim. 3, 16because he had to be manifested in the flesh,
endured,

that he might fulfill the promise made to the fathers, and while preparing the new people for himself, might demonstrate while on earth that after accomplishing the resurrection he himself will judge.
Furthermore, while teaching Israel and performing such great wonders and signs, he preached, and loved them exceedingly.

And when he chose his own apostles who were to preach his gospel, being men lawless beyond every sin—Mk. 2, 17so that he might show that he came not to call the righteous, but sinners—then he manifested himself to be the Son of God.

For if he had not come in the flesh, how οὐδ ἄν πως ℵ, οὐδ’ ἄν C, πῶς ἄν GL.could men have been saved by looking upon him, when looking upon the sun—which is destined to cease to be and is the work of his hands—they are not able to gaze directly into its rays?
Therefore the Son of God came in the flesh to this end, that he might sum up the full measure of the sins of those who persecuted his prophets to death.

To this end, then, he endured. For God says of the wound Zach. 13, 6. 7. cf. Mt. 26, 31of his flesh that it came from them: When they strike their own shepherd, then the sheep of the flock shall be destroyed.

And he himself willed to suffer thus; for it was necessary that he should suffer on a tree. Ps. 22, 40For he who prophesies of him says: Spare my Ps. 119, 120;soul from the sword, and: Pierce my flesh with nails, for assemblies of evildoers have risen up Is. 50, 8, 9against me.
And again he says: Behold, I have given my back to scourges and my cheeks to blows, and I have set my face as a solid rock.

When, then, he had fulfilled the commandment, what does he say? Who is he that contends with me? Let him oppose me; or who is he that goes to law with me? Let him draw near to the servant of the Lord.

Woe to you, for you shall all grow old like a garment, and the moth shall devour you. And again the prophet says, Is. 28, 16, cf. Rom. 9, 33; I Pet. 2,6since he was set as a strong stone for crushing: Behold, I will lay in the foundations of Zion a precious stone, chosen, a cornerstone, honorable.

Then what Is. 28, 16does he say? And whoever hopes in him ὃς ἐλπίσει ἐπ’ αὐτόν G, ὁ πιστεύων εἰς αὐτόν ℵCL, probably owing to the influence of the LXX. ἐλπίσει is covered by the following ἐλπίς.shall live forever. Is our hope then set upon a stone? Far be it! Rather, it is because the Lord has set his flesh in strength; Is. 50, 7for he says: And he set me as a solid Ps. 117, 22. 24rock.
And again the prophet says: The stone that the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner. And again he says: This is the great and wonderful day that the Lord has made.
I write to you the more simply so that you may understand—I, the devoted servant of your love. Ps. 22, 18; 118, 12
What then does the prophet say again? An assembly of evildoers encompassed me; they surrounded me like Ps. 21, 19bees around a honeycomb; and: Upon my clothing they cast lots.

Since, then, he was about to be manifested and to suffer in the flesh, his passion was manifested beforehand. For the prophet says concerning Israel: Is. 3. 9, 10, cf. Wisd. 2, 12Woe to their soul, for they have taken an evil counsel against themselves, saying: Let us bind the
righteous man, for he is inconvenient to us.

What says Exod. 33 1. 3; Lev. 20, 24the other prophet, Moses, to them? Behold, thus says the Lord God: Enter into the good land which the Lord swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and inherit it—a land flowing with milk and honey.

And what does knowledge say? Learn: Hope, it says, φησίν ℵC CL Clem. Alex. om. ℵ* G.in Jesus, who is to be manifested to you in the flesh. For man is earth that suffers, since the molding of Adam took place from the face of the earth. Exod. 33, 1. 3

What then does it mean: Into the good land, a land flowing with milk and honey? Blessed be our Lord, brethren, who has placed in us wisdom and understanding of his secrets; for the prophet speaks a parable of the Lord: who shall understand it, save one who is wise, learned, Eph. 2. 10; 4, 22-24and loves his Lord?
Since, then, he renewed us by the forgiveness of sins, he made us of another pattern, so as to have the soul of children, as though he were indeed molding us anew.

For Scripture speaks concerning us when Gen. 1, 26he says to the Son: Let us make man according to our image and likeness, and let them rule over the beasts of the earth and the birds of heaven and the fish of the sea. And the Lord said, Gen. 1, 28seeing our fair creation: Increase and multiply and fill the earth. These things were spoken to the Son.

Again I will show you how he speaks to us. λέγει CL(g), λέγει κύριος ℵ.He made a second creation in the last days;
Cf. Mt. 19, 30; 20, 16and the Lord says: Behold, I make the last things as the first. To this end, therefore, the prophet proclaimed: Exod. 33, 3Enter into a land flowing with milk and honey and have dominion over it.

See then, we have been molded anew, just as again he says in another prophet: Ezck. 11, 19; 36, 26Behold, says the Lord, I will take out of these—that is, those whom the Spirit of the Lord foresaw—their hearts of stone, and I will put in hearts of flesh; because he himself was to be manifested in flesh and to dwell in us.
For a holy temple to the Lord, my brethren, is the dwelling-place of our heart. Ps. 43, 4

For the Lord says again: And wherein shall I appear before the Lord my God and be glorified? Ps. 22, 23He says: I will confess to you in the assembly of my brethren, and I will sing to you in the midst of the assembly of the saints. Therefore we are the ones whom he brought into the good land.

What then is the milk and the honey? Because a child is first nourished with honey, and then with milk; so likewise we, being nourished by faith in the promise and by the word, shall live and have dominion over the earth.

Now we have said προειρήκαμεν ℵ, προείρπηε CG, L omits the whole sentence.above: Gen. 1, 26, 28And let them increase and multiply and rule over the fish. Who then is able now to rule over beasts or fish or birds of heaven? For we ought to perceive that to rule implies authority, so that one may command and have dominion.
If then this does not happen now, he has told us when it will: when we ourselves have been made perfect to become heirs of the covenant of the Lord.

Understand therefore, children of gladness, that the good Lord manifested all things to us beforehand, that we might know whom we ought to praise, giving thanks in everything. II Tim. 4, 1 (I. Pet. 4, 5)

If, then, the Son of God, being Lord and about to judge the living and the dead, suffered in order that his wound might give us life, let us believe that the Son of God could not suffer except for our sake. Mt. 27, 34, 48

Moreover, when crucified, he was given vinegar and gall to drink. Hear how the Lev. 23, 29priests of the temple made revelation concerning this. Since a commandment is written: Whoever does not keep the fast shall surely be put to death, the Lord commanded this because he himself too was about to offer the vessel of the Spirit as a sacrifice for our sins, so that the type established in Isaac, who was offered upon the altar, might also be fulfilled.
What then does he say in the prophet? And let them eat of the goat that is offered at the fast for all sins. Pay close attention: And let all the priests alone eat the entrails unwashed with vinegar.

To what end? Since you are about to give me gall with vinegar to drink when I am about to offer my flesh for the sins of my new people, Mt. 27, 34. 48do you alone eat, while the people fast and mourn in sackcloth and ashes—in order to show that he must suffer at their hands.
Note what he commanded: Lev. 16, 7, 9Take two fine and matching goats and offer them, and let the priest take the one for a burnt offering for sins.

And
Lev. 16, 8. 10what are they to do ποιήσωσιν ℵ, ποιήσουσιν CG.with the other? The one, he says, is accursed. Pay attention to how the type of Jesus is manifested:

And do you all spit on it and pierce it and bind the scarlet wool around its head, and so let it be cast out into the wilderness. And when this is done, the man who carries the goat leads it into the wilderness and takes off the wool and places it upon the bush called Rachel, ῥαχήλ ℵ, ῥαχίλ G, ῥαχήC.whose shoots we are accustomed to eat when we find them in the countryside; thus of the thorn-bush ῥαχοῦς ℵG, ῥαχῆς C. τῆς ῥαχοῦς can scarcely be right, but in face of the evidence can hardly be rejected.alone the fruits are sweet.

What then is this? Lev. 16, 8Pay attention: The one for the altar, and the other accursed—and why is the accursed one crowned? Because they shall see him on that Rev. 1, 7. 13day wearing the scarlet robe reaching to his feet about his flesh, and they shall say: Is not this he whom we once crucified, despising, piercing, and spitting upon him? ἐξουθενήσαμεν ἐμπτύσαντες ℵ.Truly this was he who then said that he was the Son of God.

For how Lev. 16. 7is he like that goat? For this reason the goats are alike, fine and equal, so that when they see him coming then, they may be amazed at the likeness of the goat. Behold, therefore, the type of Jesus who was to suffer.

And why do they place the wool in the midst of the thorns? It is a type of Jesus set forth for the Church, because whoever wishes to take up the scarlet wool must suffer much because the thorn is
terrible, and only through affliction can he gain possession of it. Thus, he says, those who wish to see me and lay hold of my kingdom must receive me through affliction and suffering.

Num. 19And what type do you think it is that Israel is commanded that men in whom sins are complete should offer a heifer, and after slaughtering it should burn it, and that children should then take up the ashes and put them into vessels and bind scarlet wool about a piece of wood (behold again the type of the cross and the scarlet wool) together with hyssop, and that the children should thus sprinkle the people one by one, that they may be purified from their sins?

Understand how plainly he speaks to you. The calf is Jesus; the sinful men who offer it are those who brought him to the slaughter. Then no longer men, no longer the glory of sinners. εἶτα . . . δόξα om. L.

The children who sprinkle are those who preached to us the good news of the forgiveness of sins and the purification of the heart, to whom he gave the authority of the gospel—being twelve as a testimony to the tribes, because there are twelve tribes of Israel—to preach.
And why are there three children who sprinkle? As a testimony to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because these are great before God.

And why the wool upon the wood? Because the
kingdom of Jesus is upon the wood, ξύλου ℵ ξύλῳ CS.and because those who hope in him shall live forever.

And why the wool and the hyssop together? Because in his kingdom there shall be evil and foul days, in which we shall be saved; for he too who suffers in his flesh is healed through the foulness of the hyssop.
And for this reason the things that happened thus are plain to us, but obscure to them, because they did not hear the voice of the Lord.

For again he speaks concerning the ears, how he circumcised our heart. The Lord says in the Ps. 18, 44prophet: At the hearing of the ear they obeyed me. And Is. 33, 13again he says: Those who are afar off shall hear with hearing, Jer. 4, 4they shall know what I have done. And: Be circumcised, says the Lord, in your hearts.

And again he says: Jer. 7, 2. 3Hear, O Israel, for thus says the Lord your God. Ps. 33 (34), 13; Exod, 15, 26And again the Spirit of the Lord prophesies: καὶ πάλιν . . . προφητεύει GL, om. ℵC.Who is he that desires to live forever? Let him hear with hearing the voice of my servant.

And again Is. 1, 2he says: Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord has spoken these things as a testimony. And again he says: Is. 1. 10Hear the word of the Lord, you rulers of this people. Is. 40, 3And again he says: Hear, O children, the voice of one crying in the wilderness. Therefore he circumcised our hearing, so that having heard the word we might believe.

Moreover, the circumcision in which they trusted has been abolished; for he said that circumcision was not to be of the flesh. Yet they transgressed, because an evil angel
Jer. 4, 3. 4misled them.

He says to them: Thus says the Lord your God (here I find a commandment): Do not sow among thorns; be circumcised to your Deut. 10, 16Lord. And what does he say? Circumcise your hardness of heart, and stiffen your neck no more. Jer. 9, 25. 26Take another passage: Behold, says the Lord, all the nations are uncircumcised in foreskin, but this people is uncircumcised in heart.

But you will say: Surely the people has been circumcised as a seal! Yet every Syrian and Arab and all the priests of the idols are circumcised too; do they then also belong to their covenant? Indeed, even the Egyptians practice circumcision.

Learn therefore, children of love, concerning all things richly: that Abraham, who first gave circumcision, circumcised looking forward in the Spirit to Jesus, having received the doctrines of three letters.

For it says: Gen. 17, 23, 27; 14, 14And Abraham circumcised from his household eighteen and three hundred men. What then was the knowledge given to him? Notice that he mentions the eighteen first, and after a pause says three hundred. The eighteen is iota (ten) and eta (eight): there you have Jesus. And because the cross was to have grace in the letter tau, he says also three hundred. Thus he indicates Jesus in the two letters, and in the one the cross.
He who placed the innate gift of his teaching in us knows this. No one has learned a more genuine word from me; yet I know that you are worthy.
Lev. 11; Deut. 14Now when Moses said: You shall not eat swine, nor eagle, nor hawk, nor crow, nor any fish that has no scales upon it, he received three doctrines in his understanding.
Furthermore, Deut, 4, 1. 5he says to them in Deuteronomy: And I will establish my ordinances with this people. Therefore it is not a commandment of God not to eat, but Moses spoke in the Spirit.

He spoke of the pig, then, to this end: You shall not join yourself, he means, to such men as are like pigs—χοίρων ℵ, χοίρως CG.that is, when they live in luxury they forget the Lord, but when they are in want they acknowledge the Lord; just as the pig, when it eats, does not know its master, but when it is hungry it cries out, and having received food is Lev. 11, 13-16silent again.

Neither shall you eat the eagle, nor the hawk, nor the kite, nor the crow: You shall not, he means, join yourself to or become like such men as do not know how to provide food for themselves through toil and sweat, but seize what belongs to others in their lawlessness, and lie in wait while walking as if in innocence, looking around for whom they may strip out of greed—just as these birds alone do not provide food for themselves, but sit idle and seek how they may devour the flesh of others, being pestilent in their wickedness. Lev. 11, 10

And you shall not eat, he says, the lamprey, nor the polypus, nor the cuttlefish: You shall not, he means, become like by joining yourself to κολλώμενος GL, om. ℵC.such men as are utterly
ungodly and already condemned to death, just as these fish alone, accursed, swim in the depths, not swimming about like the rest, but dwelling in the mud beneath the deep.

Moreover, Lev. 11, 5you shall not eat the hare. To what end? You shall not become, he means, a corrupter of boys, nor become like such men; because the hare adds a new anal opening every year, for as many years as it lives, so many holes it has.

Nor shall you eat the hyena: You shall not, he means, become an adulterer or a seducer, nor become like such men. To what end? Because this animal changes its nature every year and becomes at one time male Lev, 11. 29and at another time female.

And he also rightly detested the weasel: You shall not, he means, become like those whom we hear of as committing lawlessness with the mouth through uncleanness, nor join yourself to unclean women who commit lawlessness with the mouth; for this animal conceives through the mouth.
Concerning foods, then, Moses received three doctrines and spoke thus in the Spirit; but they, according to the lust of the flesh, received them as concerning eating.

David also receives knowledge of the same three doctrines Ps 1, 1and says: Blessed is the man who has not walked in the counsel of the ungodly—just as the fish go in darkness into the depths—and has not stood in the way of sinners—just as those who pretend to fear the Lord sin like the pig—and has not sat in the seat of the pestilent—just as the birds sit waiting for prey. You have now the complete teaching
concerning food as well.

Again Moses says: Lev. 11, 3; Deut. 14, 6You shall eat everything that parts the hoof and chews the cud. What does he mean? That receiving food it knows him who feeds it, and resting upon him it appears to be glad. Well did he speak, having regard to the commandment. What then does he mean? Cleave to those who fear the Lord, to those who meditate in their heart on the distinction of the word they have received, to those who speak of the ordinances of the Lord and keep them, to those who know that meditation is a work of gladness and who ruminate upon the word of the Lord. And what does "that parts the hoof" mean? That the righteous man both walks in this world and looks forward to the holy age. See how well Moses legislated!

Yet how could they grasp or understand these things? But we, having rightly understood the commandments, speak as the Lord willed; for this reason he circumcised our ears and our hearts, that we might understand these things.

Let us inquire also whether the Lord took care to reveal beforehand concerning the water and concerning the cross. Concerning the water it is written with reference to Israel, how they will not accept the baptism that brings forgiveness of sins, but will build for themselves. Jer. 2, 12. 13

For the prophet says: Be astonished, O heaven, and let the earth shudder the more at this, for this people has done two evil things: they have forsaken me,
the fountain of life, and dug for themselves a pit of death. Is. 16, 1. 2
Is my holy mountain Sinai a desert rock? For you shall be as the fledglings of a bird, fluttering away when deprived of their nest.

And again the prophet says: Is. 45. 2. 3I will go before you and level mountains, and shatter gates of bronze and break bars of iron, and I will give you dark, hidden, unseen treasures, that they may know Is. 33, 16-18that I am the Lord God.
And: You shall dwell in a lofty cave of a strong rock. And: Its water is sure; you shall see a King with glory, and your soul shall meditate on the fear of the Lord.

And Ps. 1, 3-6again in another prophet he says: And he who does these things shall be like the tree planted beside the streams of waters, which shall yield its fruit in its season, and its leaf shall not fall off, and whatever he does shall prosper.

Not so the ungodly, not so; rather they are like the chaff that the wind scatters from the face of the earth. Therefore the ungodly shall not rise up in judgment, nor sinners in the counsel of the righteous, for the Lord knows the way of the righteous, and the way of the ungodly shall perish.

Perceive how he joined the water and the cross together. For this is what he means: Blessed are those who, hoping in the cross, went down into the water; for he speaks of the reward "in its season"—then, he says, I will repay. And as for what he says now, "its leaves shall not fall off," he means this: that every word that goes forth from you through your Ps. 1, 3mouth in faith and love shall be for conversion and hope to many.

And again another prophet says: And the land of Jacob was
praised above all the earth. By this he means: Cf. Wisd. 3, 19he glorifies the vessel of his Spirit.
Then Ezek. 47, 1-12what does he say? And there was a river flowing from the right, and fair trees rose up from it; and whoever eats of them shall live forever.

This means that we go down into the water full of sins and filth, and we come up bearing fruit in our heart, having fear and hope Ezek. 47, 9in Jesus in the Spirit. And "whoever eats of these shall live forever" means this: whoever, he says, hears these things spoken and believes shall live forever.

IV Esr. 4, 33; 5, 5Similarly again he defines concerning the cross in another prophet, who says: And when shall these things be accomplished? The Lord says: When a tree shall be bent down and rise up, and when blood shall drip from wood. Once more you have a reference to the cross and to him who was to be Exod. 17, 18 ff.crucified.

And again he speaks to Moses, τῷ Μωυσῇ ℵC, ἐν τῷ Μωυσῇ GL “in Moses” i.e. in the “Pentateuch” which was spoken of as “Moses.” when Israel was being attacked by foreigners, and to remind them while under attack that they had been delivered to death because of their sins: the Spirit speaks to the heart of Moses that he should make a type of the cross and of him who was to suffer, because unless, he says, they hope in him, they shall be warred upon forever. Moses therefore piles shield upon shield in the midst of the battle, and standing higher than all, stretched out his hands, and
thus Israel prevailed again; then, whenever he lowered them, they were slain.
To what end? That they might know they cannot be saved unless they hope in him. Is. 65, 2
And again in another prophet he says: All day long I have stretched out my hands to a disobedient ἀπειθῆ ℵ ἀπειθοῦντα Cg (LXX).people that contradicts my righteous way.

Again Moses makes a type of Jesus, that he must suffer and that he himself whom they will think they have destroyed shall give life, in a sign when Israel was falling—Num. 21, 6 ff.for the Lord caused every serpent to bite them, and they were dying, since the transgression had come about through the serpent in Eve—to convince them that because of their transgression they would be delivered to the affliction of death. Deut 27. 15

Furthermore, though Moses himself had commanded: You shall have neither molten nor carved image for your god, yet he himself makes one in order to show a type of Jesus. Moses therefore makes a bronze serpent and sets it up conspicuously and summons the people by proclamation.

Coming together, then, they entreated Moses to offer prayer on their behalf for their healing. And Moses said to them: Num. 21, 8. 9Whenever, he says, any one of you is bitten, let him come to the serpent set upon the pole and hope in faith that it, though dead, is able to give life, and he shall immediately be saved. And so they did. Here again you have the glory of Jesus, for in him and unto him are all things. Num. 13, 17

What again does Moses say to Jesus (Joshua), son of Nun, giving him this name as a prophet, solely so that all the people might hear that the Father
reveals everything concerning his Son Jesus?

Moses therefore says to Jesus (Joshua), son of Nun, giving him this name Exod. 17, 14when he sent him to spy out the land: Take a book into your hands and write what the Lord says, that the Son of God will cut off by the roots all the house of Amalek in the last days.

Behold again Jesus—not son of man, but Mt. 22. 42-44Son of God, yet manifested in a type in the flesh. Since, therefore, they are going to say that Christ is the son of David, Χριστὸς υἱὸς Δαυείδ ἐστιν ℵ, ὁ Χριστὸς υἱός ἐστιν Δαυείδ CG.David himself prophesies, fearing and Ps. 110, 1understanding the error of sinners: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet. Is. 45, 1

And again Isaiah speaks thus: The Lord said to my Christ the Lord, whose right hand I have held, that nations should obey before him, and I will break in pieces the strength of kings. See how David calls Mk. 12, 37 cf. Mt. 22, 45; Luke, 20, 44him Lord, and does not call him son.
Now let us see whether this people or the former people is the heir, and whether the covenant is for us or for them.

Hear then what Scripture says concerning the people: Gen. 25, 21And Isaac prayed concerning Rebekah his wife, because she was barren; and she conceived. Gen. 25, 22-23 cf. Rom. 9, 10-12Then Rebekah went out to inquire of the Lord, and the Lord said to her: Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples are in your belly; and
one people shall surpass the other, and the greater shall serve the lesser.
You ought to perceive who Isaac is and who Rebekah is, and of whom he has shown that this people is greater than that.
And in another prophecy Jacob speaks more plainly to Gen. 48, 11Joseph his son, saying: Behold, the Lord has not deprived me of your face; bring your sons to me, that I may bless them.

And Gen. 48, 9he brought Ephraim and Manasseh, wishing Manasseh to be blessed because he was the elder; for Joseph led him to the right hand of his father Jacob. But Jacob saw in the Spirit a type Gen. 48, 13-19of the people to come; and what does it say? And Jacob crossed his hands and laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, the second and younger, and blessed him. And Joseph said to Jacob: Move your right hand to the head of Manasseh, for he is my firstborn son. And Jacob said to Joseph: I know, my child, I know; yet the greater shall serve the lesser, though this one too shall be blessed.
See of whom he has ordained that this people should be first and heir of the covenant.

If, then, it was also mentioned through Abraham, we have reached Gen. 15, 6the perfection of our knowledge. What then does he say to Abraham, when he alone believed and it was reckoned to him as righteousness? Gen. 17. 4. 5, cf. Rom. 4 12-13Behold, I have made you, Abraham, the father of nations who believe in God while uncircumcised.

Yes; yet let us see whether he has given the covenant that he swore to the fathers to give to the people. εἰ δέδωκεν ℵ, εἰ δέδωκεν ζητῶμεν C(GL); the grammar of the sentence is emended by G to ἀλλὰ τὴν διαθήκην, ἤν . . . λαῷ, εἰ δέδωκεν ζητῶμεν.He has given it; but they were not worthy to receive it because of their sins.

For the prophet says: Exod. 24, 18And Moses was fasting on Mount Sinai to receive the covenant of the Lord for the people, forty days Exod. 31, 18and forty nights. And Moses received from the Lord the two tablets written by the finger of the hand of the Lord in the Spirit; and taking them, Moses carried them down to give to the people.

And the Lord said to Exod. 32, 7-19; Deut. 9, 12-17Moses: Moses, Moses, go down quickly, for your people whom you brought out of the land of Egypt have acted lawlessly. And Moses understood that they had again made molten images for themselves, and he cast them out of his hands, χειρῶν ℵC, χειρῶν τὰς πλάκας GL.and the tablets of the covenant of the Lord were broken in pieces.

Moses indeed received it, but they were not worthy. Now learn how we received it: Moses received it as a servant, but the Lord himself gave it to us to be the people of inheritance, having endured for our sake.

And he was manifested both that they might reach the full measure of their sins, and that we might receive the covenant through the Lord Jesus who inherits it, Tit. 2, 14who was prepared for this purpose, that appearing in person he might redeem from darkness our hearts already consumed
by death and given over to the lawlessness of error, and establish a covenant in us by his word.
For it is written how the Father commands him to redeem us from darkness and prepare for himself a holy Is 42, 6. 7people.

The prophet therefore says: I, the Lord your God, have called you in righteousness, and I will hold your hand and strengthen you, and I have given you for a covenant of a people, for a light to the nations, to open the eyes of the blind and to bring out from bonds those who are fettered, and from the prison house those sitting in darkness. We know, therefore, whence we were redeemed. Is. 49. 6. 7

Again the prophet says: Behold, I have set you for a light to the nations, that you may be for salvation unto the end of the earth; thus says the Lord God who redeemed you. Is. 61, 1. 2, cf. Luke, 4, 17. 19

And again the prophet says: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to preach grace to the humble; ταπεινοῖς χάριν G, ταπεινοῖς L, πτωχοῖς ℵ (LXX) om. C.he has sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to proclaim an acceptable year of the Lord and a day of recompense, to comfort all who mourn.

Furthermore, concerning the Sabbath also it is written in the Ten Words in which he spoke on Mount Exod 20, 8; Deut. 5, 12, cf. Ps. 23, 4Sinai face to face with Moses: Sanctify also the Sabbath of the Lord with clean hands and a clean heart.

And in another place he says: If
Jer 17. 24. 25, cf. Ex. 31, 13-17my sons keep the Sabbath, then I will bestow my mercy upon them.
He speaks of the Sabbath Gen. 2. 2at the beginning of creation: And God made in six days the works of his hands, and finished on the seventh day, and rested on Gen. 2, 2it and sanctified it.

Pay attention, children, to what "he finished in six days" means. This means that in six thousand years the Lord will bring all things to an end; for with him a day signifies Ps. 90, 4; II Pet. 3, 8a thousand years. He himself bears witness to me, saying: Behold, the day of the Lord shall be as a thousand years. Therefore, children, in six days—that is, in six thousand years—all things shall be brought to an end. Gen 2, 2

And he rested on the seventh day. This means: when his Son comes and abolishes the time of the Lawless One, and judges the ungodly, and changes the sun and the moon and the stars, then he shall truly Ex. 20, 8rest on the seventh day.

Furthermore he says: You shall sanctify it with clean hands and a clean heart. If, then, anyone is now able, being clean in heart, to sanctify the day that God sanctified, we have been wholly deceived.

Behold, then, that we shall truly rest and sanctify it only when we ourselves are able to do so, having been justified and having received the promise, when lawlessness is no more and all things have been made new by the Lord; then we shall be able to sanctify it, having been sanctified ourselves first. Is 1, 13

Furthermore he says to them: Your new moons and sabbaths I cannot endure. See how he speaks: it is not your present sabbaths that are acceptable to me, but the one that I have made, in which, having given rest to all things, I shall make the beginning of an eighth day,
that is, the beginning of another world.
Wherefore we also keep the eighth day for gladness, on which Jesus too rose from the dead and, having been manifested, ascended into the heavens.

I will also speak to you further concerning the temple, how the wretched people went astray and placed their hope in the building, as if it were the house of God, rather than in their God who made them.

For almost like the Gentiles they consecrated him in the temple. Yet learn how the Lord speaks in abolishing it: Is 40, 12Who has measured heaven with a span or the earth with his palm? Is. 66, 1Have not I? says the Lord: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool of my feet; what house will you build for me, or what is the place of my rest? You know now that their hope was vain.
Furthermore Is. 49, 17he says again: Behold, those who tore down this temple shall themselves build it.
This is coming to pass; for because they went to war, it was torn down by their enemies, and now the very servants of their enemies will rebuild it.

Again, it was revealed that the city and the temple and the people of Israel were to be delivered up. Enoch 89, 55, 66, 67For Scripture says: And it shall come to pass in the last days that the Lord will deliver up the sheep of the pasture and the sheepfold and their tower to destruction. And it came to pass just as the Lord spoke.

Let us inquire, however, whether there is a temple of God. There is—where he himself says Dan. 9, 24-27 ?he makes and completes it. For it is written: And
it shall come to pass, when the week is being completed, that a temple of God shall be built gloriously in the name of the Lord.

I find, then, that there is a temple. How then shall it be built in the name of the Lord? Learn: before we believed in God, the dwelling-place of our heart was corrupt and weak, truly like a temple built by hand, because it was full of idolatry and was a house of demons through Dan. 9, 24-27 ?doing whatever was contrary to God.

Yet it shall be built in the name of the Lord. Take heed, therefore, that the temple of the Lord may be built gloriously. How? Learn: having received the forgiveness of sins and having hoped in the name, we became new, being created again from the beginning; wherefore God truly dwells in us, in our dwelling-place.

How? His word of faith, his calling of promise, the wisdom of the ordinances, the commandments of the teaching—he himself prophesying in us, he himself dwelling in us, opening to us who were enslaved to death τοὺς . . . δεδουλωμένους CGL, τοῖς δεδουλωμένοις ℵ (probably a correction of the unexpected accusative).the door of the temple (which is the mouth), and granting us repentance—leads us into the incorruptible temple.

For he who longs to be saved looks not to the man, but to him who dwells and speaks in him, amazed at him because he has never before heard such words from the mouth of the speaker nor ever himself desired to hear them. This is a spiritual temple being built for the Lord.

So far as it was possible to make plain to you with simplicity, my soul hopes that according to my desire I have not omitted τῇ ἐπιθυμίᾳ μου μὴ παραλελοιπέναι τι τῶν ἀνηκόντων εἰς σωτηρίαν ℵCG, μὴ παραλελοιπέναι τι ℵ*G.anything pertaining to salvation.

For if I should write to you concerning things present or things to come, you would not understand, because they lie in parables. So much, then, for these matters. With the addition of the doxology the Latin version comes here to an end.

Now let us pass on to another kind of knowledge and teaching. There are two ways of teaching and authority: that of light and that of darkness. And there is a great difference between the two ways; for over the one are stationed light-bringing angels of God, and over the other angels of Satan.
And the one is Lord from eternity and unto eternity, while the other is ruler of the present time of lawlessness.
The way of light, then, is this: if anyone wishes to travel the road to the appointed place, let him be zealous in his works. The knowledge given to us for walking in it is as follows.

You shall love him who made you; you shall fear him who formed you;
you shall glorify him who redeemed you from death. You shall be single-minded in heart and rich in spirit. You shall not join yourself to those who walk in the way of death; you shall hate everything that is not pleasing to God; you shall hate all hypocrisy; you shall not forsake the commandments of the Lord.

You shall not exalt yourself, but shall be humble-minded in all things; you shall not take glory to yourself. You shall not take evil counsel against your neighbor; you shall not give boldness to your soul.

You shall not commit fornication, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not corrupt boys. Let not the word of God go forth from you in the uncleanness of any. You shall not show partiality in rebuking anyone for a transgression. You shall be gentle, you shall be quiet, you shall tremble at the words you have heard. You shall not bear a grudge against your brother.

You shall not be of two minds whether a thing shall be Deut. 5, 11or not. You shall not take the name of the Lord in vain. You shall love your neighbor more than your own soul. You shall not murder a child by abortion, nor again kill it after it is born. You shall not withhold your hand from your son or from your daughter, but from youth you shall teach them the fear of God.

You shall not covet what belongs to your neighbor; you shall not be greedy. Neither shall you cleave with your soul to the haughty, but you shall associate with the humble and righteous. The events that befall you, you shall accept as good, knowing that nothing happens without God.

You shall not be double-minded or talkative. γλωσσώδης ℵ, δίγλωσσος CG; G also adds παγίς γὰρ θανάτου ἐστιν ἡ διγλωσσία (from Apost. Comst.) “for to be double-tongued is the mare of death.”
You shall be subject to masters as to a type of God, in modesty and fear. You shall not give orders in bitterness to your male slave or maidservant who hope in the same God, lest they cease to fear the God who is over both; for he came not to call according to outward station, but those whom the Spirit prepared.

You shall share all things with your neighbor and shall not say that they are your own; for if you are sharers in what is incorruptible, how much more in what is corruptible? You shall not be hasty of tongue, for the mouth is a snare of death. So far as you can, you shall keep yourself pure for the sake of your soul.

Do not be one who stretches out his hands to receive, yet draws them back from giving. Deut. 32, 10; Ps. 17, 8, Prov. 7, 2You shall love as the apple of your eye everyone who speaks to you the word of the Lord.

You shall remember the day of judgment night and day, and you shall seek out daily the faces of the saints, either laboring by word and going forth to exhort and meditating to save a soul by the word, or working with your hands for the ransom of your sins.

You shall not hesitate Deut. 12, 32to give, nor murmur when giving; and you shall know who is the good repayer of the reward. You shall keep what you have received, neither adding nor taking away. To the end Deut. 1, 16; Prov. 31, 9you shall hate what is evil. You shall judge righteously.

You shall not cause division, but shall reconcile those who contend by bringing them together. You shall confess your sins. You shall not come to prayer with an evil conscience. This is the way of light.

But the way of the Black One is crooked and full of cursing; for it is a way of eternal death with punishment, in which are the things that destroy their soul: idolatry, boldness, arrogance of power, hypocrisy, double-heartedness, adultery, murder, robbery, pride, transgression, deceit, malice, self-will, sorcery, magic, greed, and lack of the fear of God;

persecutors of the good, haters of truth, lovers of falsehood, not knowing the reward of righteousness, Rom. 12, 9not cleaving to what is good nor to righteous judgment, paying no heed to widow and orphan, keeping watch not for the fear of God but for evil, from whom gentleness and endurance are far and Ps. 4, 2distant, lovers of vanity, Is. 1, 23pursuing recompense, having no mercy on the poor, not toiling for the oppressed, prone to slander, not knowing him who made them, murderers of children, destroyers of God's handiwork, turning away from the needy, oppressing the afflicted, advocates of the rich, lawless judges of the poor, altogether sinful.

It is good, therefore, for one who has learned the ordinances of the Lord, as many as are written, to walk in them; for he who does these things shall be glorified in the kingdom of God, whereas he who chooses the other shall perish together with his works. For this reason there is a resurrection,
for this reason there is a recompense.
I entreat those who are in high station, if you receive any counsel of good intent from me: you have among yourselves those to whom you may do good; do not fail them.
The day is at hand in which Is. 40, 10all things shall perish together with the Evil One; the Lord is at hand, and his reward.
Again and again I entreat you: be good lawgivers to yourselves, remain faithful counselors to yourselves, put away from you all hypocrisy.
And may God, who is Lord of the whole world, grant you wisdom, understanding, skill, knowledge of his ordinances, and endurance.
Be taught of God, seeking out what the Lord requires of you, and act so that you may be found worthy in the day of judgment.
And if there is any remembrance of good, remember me as you meditate on these things, so that both my desire and my watchfulness may result in some good. I entreat you, asking a favor.
While the good vessel is still with you, do not fail in any of these things yourselves, αὐτῶν GL, ἑαυτῶν ℵC.but continually seek them out and fulfill every commandment; for they are worthy.

Wherefore I have been the more eager to write to you from what I was able, to gladden you. Farewell, children of love and peace. The Lord of glory and of all grace be with your spirit. The Epistle of Barnabas.
